correctness.rationale: Every Boolean congruence is x~_J y iff x xor y subset J. For nonzero J, choose a in J and compare S to S xor {a}; unary compatibility forces T xor {a} subset J and thus T subset J. Conversely T subset J ensures unary compatibility for all pairs, so the ambient congruences are exactly J=empty or J containing T, 1+2^(n-|T|). A Boolean partition subalgebra is stable either when S is absent (identity restriction) or when S and T are both block unions (one-point restriction). In the first case a nonzero local support I extends iff no partition block outside I is wholly inside T; in the second the support extension J=I always works. This gives CEP for S empty (all subalgebras contain zero) and for coatom S (singleton T cannot be an entire uncollapsed block if S absent). If S is nonempty noncoatom, choose s in S,t in T,u outside S and {t}; partition with singleton {t}, doubleton {s,u}, rest singletons. The identity local operator allows collapse of {s,u}, but ambient nonzero support must also collapse {t}. Enumeration yields 3^n-2^n perturbations, 2^n+n-1 CEP, n(n+1)/2 isomorphism types and n+1 CEP types. Independently checked every stable partition, congruence ideal and perturbation for n=2,3,4: (CEP,nonCEP)=(5,0),(10,9),(19,46).
